cur:catacombs-adoration-magi-sarcophagus.summary: The Virgin, veiled and seated, holds up the Child, who stretches out his hands to receive the gifts of three Magi in short tunics and Phrygian caps; a star shines above, and the heads of their camels appear behind them. The Child's eager gesture makes this one of the most tender versions of the scene in early Christian sculpture.
facts: Commons states that the panel comes from a Roman sarcophagus found in the cemetery of Sant'Agnese in Rome.
The camels' heads in the background are a characteristic detail of Roman Epiphany scenes.

cur:manuscripts-grandval-bible-christ-in.summary: Christ, youthful and haloed, sits on a globe within a blue-grey mandorla set in a large lozenge, blessing and holding an open book; the eagle, lion, ox and angel of the evangelists occupy the points of the lozenge, and the four evangelists stand in the corners, two of them looking up toward him. Pale bands of sky and small trees give the page an airy, almost classical calm.
facts: The Moutier-Grandval Bible is a one-volume Bible of the whole Vulgate as revised by Alcuin of York, and one of three surviving illustrated Bibles made at Tours (British Library description on Commons).
Its four full-page miniatures — Genesis, Exodus, the Majestas Domini and the Apocalypse — form one of the classic Carolingian Bible cycles.
